name: Avici Card
summary: Avici is a secured Visa credit card backed by your own USDC: you keep your funds in your wallet, and Avici gives you a credit line that matches your collateral. It charges no transaction fees or FX markup, with a US$15 virtual Platinum card or a Signature tier with Visa Signature benefits. It is available in about 50 countries and 31 US states.

fees.topup: Free (Visa may add a 0.4% to 1% cross-border fee on non-USD spend)

limits.dailySpend: No fixed limit; set by Avici from your collateral
limits.monthlySpend: No fixed limit; set by Avici from your collateral
limits.atmWithdrawal: Up to 3 per day; US$1,000 per withdrawal, US$3,000 per day

kyc.notes: Verification runs through Sumsub: choose your account type and country of residence, enter personal details, upload an ID document and complete a liveness check. The card fee is charged before verification; request a refund from support if you do not pass.

pros: No transaction fees and no FX markup from Avici
You keep your USDC in your own wallet as collateral instead of pre-loading the card
Works with Apple Pay and Google Pay at no extra cost
Signature tier adds Visa Signature benefits and free ATM withdrawals
Top up with any token; Avici swaps it to USDC automatically
cons: Card fee (US$15 to US$75) is charged before identity verification
Visa may add a 0.4% to 1% cross-border fee on non-USD spending
Available in only about 50 countries and 31 US states
Avici can change or cut the credit limit at any time

faq.question: How does the Avici card work?
faq.answer: Avici is a secured credit card: your USDC stays in your wallet as collateral, and Visa gives you a credit line with matching spending power. Visa can only take funds when there is a proven card spend.

faq.question: How much does the Avici card cost?
faq.answer: A virtual Platinum card costs US$15 (extra ones US$10) and a physical Platinum card US$50, both one-off. Signature costs US$30 for the first year then US$20 a year (virtual), or US$75 then US$20 a year from year two (physical).

faq.question: What fees does the Avici card charge?
faq.answer: Avici charges no transaction fee and no FX markup, but Visa may add a 0.4% to 1% cross-border fee on non-USD spending. ATM withdrawals cost US$1 + 0.65% on Platinum and are free on Signature.

faq.question: Does Avici require KYC?
faq.answer: Yes. Verification runs through Sumsub and includes an ID document and a liveness check. The card fee is charged before verification, so request a refund from support if you do not pass.

faq.question: Where is the Avici card available?
faq.answer: In about 50 countries, including Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Japan, Mexico, Singapore, the UAE and 31 US states. It is not available to residents of China, India, Russia, Turkey, Vietnam, Israel and other restricted countries.

faq.question: Does Avici pay cashback?
faq.answer: Not on purchases. Avici's rewards come through its referral programme, which pays referrers a share of referred users' eligible spending.

availabilityNotes: Avici lists the countries where its card is available; residents of the restricted list cannot use it, and the card cannot be used for spending in Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria, Ukraine or Venezuela. In the United States only these states are supported for personal accounts: Alabama, Alaska, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Hawaii, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Maine, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Texas, Utah, Virginia, West Virginia and Wyoming. Avici's business-account region table differs from the card list, so confirm in the app before paying the card fee.
howToGet: Sign up in the Avici app with your email.
Choose a card (Platinum or Signature, virtual or physical) and pay the card fee in USDC.
Complete Sumsub verification: account type, country of residence, personal details, ID document and liveness check.
Deposit USDC as collateral, or top up with another token and let Avici swap it to USDC.
Add the card to Apple Pay or Google Pay and set per-card spending limits in the card settings.
